questions.q: To cast a gel for DNA electrophoresis, a technician needs to prepare $40 \text{ mL}$ of a $1.5\% \text{ (w/v)}$ agarose solution. How many grams of agarose powder should be weighed out?
questions.explain:
A weight-to-volume percentage (w/v) represents the number of grams of solute per $100 \text{ mL}$ of solution.

A $1.5\% \text{ (w/v)}$ solution contains $1.5 \text{ g}$ per $100 \text{ mL}$. To find the amount for $40 \text{ mL}$, set up a proportion:
$$ \frac{1.5 \text{ g}}{100 \text{ mL}} = \frac{x \text{ g}}{40 \text{ mL}} $$
$$ 100x = 60 $$
$$ x = 0.6 \text{ g} $$

questions.q: A standard operating procedure (SOP) requires $500 \text{ mL}$ of a $70\% \text{ (v/v)}$ ethanol solution to sanitize biological safety cabinets. Assuming you are starting with $100\% \text{ absolute ethanol}$, which of the following describes the correct preparation method?
options: Measure $350 \text{ mL}$ of ethanol and add it to exactly $500 \text{ mL}$ of water.
Measure $350 \text{ mL}$ of ethanol and bring the total volume up to $500 \text{ mL}$ with water.
Measure $70 \text{ mL}$ of ethanol and bring the total volume up to $500 \text{ mL}$ with water.
Measure $35 \text{ mL}$ of ethanol and add it to $465 \text{ mL}$ of water.
questions.explain:
A volume-to-volume percentage (v/v) indicates the volume of solute per $100 \text{ mL}$ of the **total** solution. 

For a $70\% \text{ (v/v)}$ solution, you need $70 \text{ mL}$ of ethanol for every $100 \text{ mL}$ of final volume. 
$$ \frac{70 \text{ mL}}{100 \text{ mL}} \times 500 \text{ mL} = 350 \text{ mL of ethanol} $$

To ensure the final concentration is perfectly accurate, you measure $350 \text{ mL}$ of ethanol and "bring to volume" (q.s.) with water until the **total volume** reaches $500 \text{ mL}$. Adding exactly $500 \text{ mL}$ of water (Option 'a') would result in an incorrect total volume of roughly $850 \text{ mL}$.

questions.q: A technician dissolves $5.0 \text{ g}$ of sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) powder into distilled water, adjusting the final total volume to $200 \text{ mL}$. What is the final weight-to-volume percentage ($\text{w/v}\%$) of this SDS solution?
questions.explain:
The formula for weight-to-volume percentage (w/v) is:
$$ \% \text{ (w/v)} = \left( \frac{\text{Mass of Solute (g)}}{\text{Total Volume of Solution (mL)}} \right) \times 100 $$

Plugging in the values:
$$ \% \text{ (w/v)} = \left( \frac{5.0 \text{ g}}{200 \text{ mL}} \right) \times 100 $$
$$ \% \text{ (w/v)} = 0.025 \times 100 = 2.5\% $$

questions.q: To create a membrane-washing buffer for a Western blot, a student needs to make $2.0 \text{ Liters}$ of a $0.1\% \text{ (v/v)}$ Tween-20 solution. How many milliliters ($\text{mL}$) of pure liquid Tween-20 detergent should be added to the mixture?
questions.explain:
A $0.1\% \text{ (v/v)}$ solution contains $0.1 \text{ mL}$ of solute per $100 \text{ mL}$ of solution. 

First, convert the total target volume from liters to milliliters:
$$ 2.0 \text{ Liters} = 2000 \text{ mL} $$

Next, set up the proportion:
$$ \frac{0.1 \text{ mL}}{100 \text{ mL}} = \frac{x \text{ mL}}{2000 \text{ mL}} $$
$$ x = 0.001 \times 2000 $$
$$ x = 2.0 \text{ mL} $$

The student must pipet $2.0 \text{ mL}$ of pure Tween-20 into the total $2.0 \text{ L}$ solution.

questions.q: A standard ELISA protocol requires the preparation of $100 \text{ mL}$ of a $5\% \text{ (w/v)}$ Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) blocking buffer. If the laboratory's precision analytical balance is currently calibrated to display mass in milligrams ($\text{mg}$), what value must the balance read when weighing out the required BSA powder?
questions.explain:
A $5\% \text{ (w/v)}$ solution inherently means $5 \text{ grams}$ of solute per $100 \text{ mL}$ of solution.

Since the protocol directly asks for a total volume of $100 \text{ mL}$, exactly $5 \text{ grams}$ of BSA powder is required. 

Next, perform a metric unit conversion from grams to milligrams:
$$ 1 \text{ gram} = 1000 \text{ milligrams} $$
$$ 5 \text{ grams} = 5 \times 1000 = 5000 \text{ mg} $$

questions.q: A standard laboratory stock of sodium chloride (NaCl) is kept at a $10\% \text{ (w/v)}$ concentration. If an assay protocol calls for the addition of exactly $2.5 \text{ g}$ of NaCl, how many milliliters ($\text{mL}$) of this stock solution must the technician dispense?
questions.explain:
A $10\% \text{ (w/v)}$ solution means there are $10 \text{ grams}$ of solute in every $100 \text{ mL}$ of solution. 

We can set up a simple proportion to solve for the unknown volume ($V$):
$$ \frac{10 \text{ g}}{100 \text{ mL}} = \frac{2.5 \text{ g}}{V \text{ mL}} $$
Cross-multiply and solve for $V$:
$$ 10 \times V = 250 $$
$$ V = 25.0 \text{ mL} $$
Dispensing $25.0 \text{ mL}$ of the stock will provide exactly $2.5 \text{ g}$ of NaCl.

questions.q: A technician needs to prepare $250 \text{ mL}$ of a $10\% \text{ (v/v)}$ bleach solution to decontaminate a biological safety cabinet. The laboratory provides a bottle of standard $100\% $ concentrated laboratory bleach. Which of the following procedures correctly prepares this solution?
options: Mix $10 \text{ mL}$ of concentrated bleach with $240 \text{ mL}$ of deionized water.
Mix $25 \text{ mL}$ of concentrated bleach with $250 \text{ mL}$ of deionized water.
Mix $25 \text{ mL}$ of concentrated bleach with $225 \text{ mL}$ of deionized water.
Mix $250 \text{ mL}$ of concentrated bleach with $10 \text{ mL}$ of deionized water.
questions.explain:
A $10\% \text{ (v/v)}$ solution requires $10\% $ of the total final volume to be the solute (bleach).

First, find the required volume of bleach:
$$ 0.10 \times 250 \text{ mL} = 25 \text{ mL of bleach} $$

The remainder of the volume must be the solvent (water) to reach the $250 \text{ mL}$ final mark:
$$ 250 \text{ mL total} - 25 \text{ mL bleach} = 225 \text{ mL water} $$

Therefore, the correct mixture is $25 \text{ mL}$ bleach + $225 \text{ mL}$ water (Option 'c').
